correctness.rationale: The product on a_i is a_i a_j=a_(2j-i mod 4). In the characteristic-free basis p=a0, q=a1, u=a0−a2, v=a1−a3, J=span(u,v) is the intrinsic right annihilator and the two-dimensional quotient is the left-zero algebra with augmentation. Solving x²=x via parity masses E,O yields zero plus three affine idempotent lines in characteristic ≠2 and zero plus two disjoint affine planes in characteristic 2. For odd characteristic, the two distinct right characters on J prevent shears and force the quotient action to identity or swap, with independent scalings of u,v: Aut=(K×)²⋊C2. In characteristic two, the multiplication-defect equations restrict quotient and J maps to simultaneous swap/identity but admit every additive shear Hom(K²,K²), so Aut=(K⁴,+)⋊C2, with transitivity on nonzero idempotents. Independent direct exhaustive multiplication tests over F2 and F3 reproduce nonzero idempotent/automorphism pairs (8,32),(7,8); general result is algebraic, not finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The smallest even-half-order dihedral quandle ring exhibits a genuine four-dimensional unipotent automorphism jump in characteristic two, tied to a geometric dimension jump of the idempotent locus. The exact two groups, orbit transitivity and finite-field cardinalities fill a structurally motivated missing case rather than a small numerical example.
